newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli dollar bonds end higher in mixed market.
newsitem.headline: Israeli dollar bonds end higher in mixed market.

text.p: Israeli dollar-linked bonds rose strongly on Monday in response to the shekel's weakening against the dollar in an otherwise mixed market, traders said.
* Bank of Israel short-term Makam bills: +0.06 pct to 107.61
Volume including Makams was 215 million shekels.

"Dollar-linked bonds were on a clear rising trend following the rise of the dollar against the shekel. But volume (for dollar-linked bonds) was a low 14.7 million shekels, which indicates that players were not so willing to sell and buyers were not aggressive enough," said Adam Reuter of Financial Immunities.
The shekel representative rate was fixed at 3.5690 against the dollar, compared with 3.5530 on Friday.
Trading in other bonds was mixed. CPI-linked bonds closed lower led by seven to 10-year bonds, while unlinked bonds posted small rises, Reuter said.
"There is a lot of uncertainty in the market about inflation and about the effects of the rise of the dollar on inflation. The players don't really know where to go," he said.

"Because the high dollar is seen influencing inflation, the higher consumer price indices expected in the coming months are pushing some traders into CPI-linked bonds. But unlinked bonds are also rising because their yields are attractive to the private investor," said a trader at Israel Discount Bank.
Yields on one-year unlinked bonds were 12.7-12.8. percent and on one-year Makams 12.8 percent, he said.
The Discount trader added that the appointment of Yaacov Neeman as finance minister had no impact on trading.

Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu named Neeman to the finance portfolio on Monday morning. National Infrastructure Minister Ariel Sharon, distrusted by the capital markets, had been the leading candidate for the post.
Note: Makams are zero-coupon unlinked certificates with durations of three months to one year. The Bank of Israel issues Makams to absorb liquidity.
